results.controlIntent: a. Use internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records; and b. Record those time stamps for audit records such that the time stamps meet [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] and satisfy one or more of the following: use Coordinated Universal Time; have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time; include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both CloudTrail audit records retrieved for the churn-predictor-endpoint use ISO 8601 timestamps with the 'Z' (UTC) suffix, satisfying AU-8.b's requirement to use Coordinated Universal Time. The timestamps (e.g., '2025-12-01T11:00:00Z' and '2026-03-15T14:22:00Z') are generated by AWS CloudTrail's internal system clocks, satisfying AU-8.a. Granularity is at the second level, which is typical for CloudTrail and generally meets standard organizational requirements. Confidence is medium rather than high because: (1) no organization-defined granularity policy was available to confirm second-level precision is explicitly sufficient, and (2) only CloudTrail events were assessed — other audit log sources (e.g., SageMaker model monitor, application-level logs) were not available for review.
gaps: Organization-defined granularity of time measurement policy not available — cannot confirm whether second-level precision meets the stated requirement
Only CloudTrail events were assessed; other audit log sources (SageMaker model monitor, inference logs, application logs) were not retrievable and may have different timestamp behaviors
No evidence of NTP/time-sync configuration for underlying compute to confirm internal system clocks are synchronized to an authoritative time source
